questions.question: A client sends If-None-Match with a matching ETag and gets a 304. What has been saved?
options: The database query and handler execution
Bandwidth, because no response body is sent; the handler still ran
questions.explanation: Express generates the ETag from the response body, so the handler runs as normal. Only the body transfer is skipped. Cache-Control max-age is what avoids the request entirely.

questions.question: Which Cache-Control value is appropriate for an authenticated endpoint returning a user's bank details?
questions.explanation: no-store forbids any cache from keeping the response. Marking per-user data public lets a CDN serve it to other users.

questions.question: When is Redis preferred over an in-memory Map for application caching?
options: When the app runs multiple instances and they need a shared cache that survives restarts
When you need the absolute lowest latency on a single process
When you want to avoid setting TTLs
Redis is never preferred; in-memory is always better
questions.explanation: An in-memory cache is per process and lost on restart. Redis is shared by all instances and supports expiry natively, at the cost of a network hop.

questions.question: An endpoint loads 20 orders, then loops and queries each order's customer separately. What is this and how do you fix it with Prisma?
options: A memory leak; fix it with compression
A race condition; fix it with a transaction
An N+1 query problem; fix it by loading the relation with include (or one batched in-query)
Cache stampede; fix it with ETags
questions.explanation: One list query plus one query per item is N+1. Prisma's include or select on the relation, or a single where id in [...] query, loads related rows in a batch.
